correctness.rationale: Let alpha=1/lambda and beta=sqrt(1-alpha²), so 0<beta≤alpha. Circular arcs, vertical open facets, and corners exhaust the clipped disk boundary. On circular smooth arcs the Birkhoff direction is a rotated radius; if s≤alpha the reverse distance is 1, otherwise it is alpha/[s(alpha s+beta c)]≥2alpha/(1+alpha)>alpha via the exact largest eigenvalue (1+alpha)/2. On facets x=(alpha,t), |t|<beta, quotient distance alpha/sqrt(t²+alpha²)≥alpha. At a corner (alpha,beta), every Birkhoff direction is (1,-r)/sqrt(1+r²), r≥alpha/beta, including r=∞, and distance is (beta+alpha r)/sqrt(1+r²), decreasing from 1 to alpha. The limiting y=(0,-1) attains alpha, giving eps=sqrt(1-alpha²). Endpoint lambda=sqrt2 and limit lambda↓1 are consistent; no second-regime assertion.

No claim is made for the second regime.
